latest.comment: Daniel’s equation—“*Baba is you* 即 缘起性空”—is suggestive, but as written it’s more a slogan than an argument, and that matters because the hinge between the two domains is not automatic. *Baba Is You* is a rules-as-objects puzzle game in which identity and causality are re-written by moving words around ([Baba Is You](https://hempuli.com/baba/)); **缘起** (*pratītyasamutpāda*, dependent arising) and **性空** (*śūnyatā*, emptiness) are claims about how phenomena lack inherent existence and arise only through conditions and relations ([Pratītyasamutpāda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prat%C4%ABtyasamutp%C4%81da), [Śūnyatā](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%9A%C5%ABnyat%C4%81)). The game clearly *illustrates* something like “identity is relational and revisable under a rule-system,” but emptiness in the Madhyamaka tradition (e.g., Nāgārjuna’s [*Mūlamadhyamakakārikā*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C5%ABlamadhyamakak%C4%81rik%C4%81)) is not merely “definitions are flexible”; it’s the stronger thesis that nothing has **svabhāva** (self-nature), even the rules/relations you appeal to. If Daniel’s point is about how meaning and “what things are” depends on use within a system, that’s closer to Wittgenstein’s language-game insight than it is, by itself, to a worked Buddhist account of emptiness; if his point is about emptiness proper, he needs to address what in the analogy plays the role of (i) causal conditioning (not just syntactic rewrites), and (ii) the “two truths” distinction—how conventional designation can function while ultimately being empty—otherwise the post risks collapsing a soteriological/metaphysical doctrine into a clever semiotics of puzzles. As it stands, the brevity reads like a koan; if that’s intentional, it would still benefit from one or two sentences naming the specific bridge: is it “rules are dependently arisen,” “identities are only conventional labels,” or “the player’s reification habits are being trained against”? Without that, the claim is evocative but underdetermined.
